reading.ar: يبدأ التقادم من تاريخ الاستحقاق، ويسأل عنه المحامي ولو كان العقد حديثا.
reading.en: Limitation starts on the due date, which the lawyer is asked for even when the contract is recent.

reading.ar: لا يسبق الاستحقاق العقد المنشئ للالتزام، فتعد الدعوى في أجلها متى كان العقد أحدث من المدة.
reading.en: The due date cannot precede the contract that created the obligation, so the claim is in time whenever the contract is more recent than the period.

protectiveReading.ar: السؤال عن تاريخ الاستحقاق وعدم الحكم بأن الدعوى في أجلها قبل معرفته؛ وبعد إدخاله يحسب الأجل وينبه قرب آخر يوم منه.
protectiveReading.en: Ask for the due date and do not report the claim in time before it is known; once it is given, the deadline is counted and warns near its last day.

checklist.item: Basis: Law 90-11 of 21 April 1990 on labour relations, the articles on termination and dismissal (art. 66 grounds of termination; art. 73 dismissal for serious fault and its list; art. 73-1 the disciplinary procedure: written, reasoned notice and hearing of the worker; art. 73-2 notice period; art. 73-3 dismissal in breach of the procedure; art. 73-4 dismissal without real and serious cause) as amended by Law 91-29 and Ordinance 96-21.
checklist.note: The store has 73 (law 91-29: serious faults and their list), 73-1 (criteria for describing the serious fault), 73-2 (the procedure: internal regulation, written notification, hearing), 73-3 (any individual dismissal in breach of the law is abusive, the employer proves the contrary), 73-4 (ordinance 96-21: remedies for a procedural breach in ¶1, for a breach of 73 in ¶2 and ¶3, cassation in ¶4). Article 66 (grounds of termination) and the notice-period article are not in the store: requested.

checklist.item: Is the plaintiff a worker under a contract of employment governed by Law 90-11, and not a civil servant (Ordinance 06-03, administrative courts) or a member of a category excluded by art. 3 or 4 of Law 90-11 (military, magistrates, special statutes)?
checklist.note: Labour-relations 1, 2 and 3 are in the store (2 and 3 imported from the modules); ordinance 06-03 and labour-relations 4 are not (requested). Article 4 (Official Journal 1990 issue 17 page 563) lets regulations set a specific regime for listed categories notwithstanding the law: open point o10. Free-zone operators: open point o13.

checklist.item: Element: the employment relation exists and its start date (contract, pay slips, social-security affiliation; the contract may be proved by any means, art. 10 of Law 90-11).
checklist.note: Labour-relations 10 (proof of the contract by any means) is not in the store: requested. The element rests on labour-relations 1 and 2, civil-code 323 and CPCA 500.

checklist.item: Element: the dismissal by the employer and its date (dismissal letter, or a factual dismissal: refusal of access, stopping of pay).
checklist.note: The dismissal date is held in the proposed slot dismissal_date; the limitation runs through the imported periods items from the due date or the harmful act (open point o1).

checklist.item: Element: the fault relied on by the employer is not a serious fault within art. 73, or the employer cannot prove it; who bears the burden of proving the fault and the regularity of the procedure (the employer, by my memory of art. 73-4 and case law).
checklist.note: The burden is in 73-3 ¶1: the employer proves the contrary; 73-1 ¶1 sets what the employer's description of the fault must weigh. The list of 73 ¶2 is not closed («على الخصوص», b3); further serious faults are defined in other laws (open point o8) and by the internal regulation (open point o7).

checklist.item: Element: the procedure of art. 73-1 (written notification of the decision, hearing of the worker, assistance by a worker of his choice) was not respected, and the internal regulation's procedure.
checklist.note: The procedure is in 73-2 ¶1 and ¶2 (internal regulation, written notification, hearing, the worker may bring a colleague).

checklist.item: Distinguish the two sanctions: procedural irregularity (art. 73-3: annulment and order to follow the procedure, plus compensation not below the monthly salary?) versus abusive dismissal on the merits (art. 73-4: reinstatement with acquired advantages, or if either party refuses, compensation not less than six months' salary, without prejudice to other damages).
checklist.note: Both remedies are in 73-4: ¶1 for a procedural breach (annulment, order to carry out the procedure, compensation not less than the pay), ¶2 and ¶3 for a breach of 73 (reinstatement or, if a party refuses, compensation not less than six months' pay). A procedure-only challenge stays inside this claim (73-3 ¶1: every individual dismissal in breach of the law; 73-4 ¶1), with requests r4 and r5; the former boundary n1 that sent it outside was removed by the verifier (attack adv-12).

checklist.item: Request: reinstatement in the post with the advantages acquired; the employer or the worker may refuse reinstatement, which turns the remedy into compensation.
Request: compensation not less than six months of salary, plus further damages if any; the amount of the salary must be stated.

Accessory requests: unpaid wages, notice-period compensation, dismissal indemnity (art. 73-2 or collective agreement), work certificate, interest, costs, provisional execution of right for wages (Law 90-04).
checklist.note: Wage arrears bring in the imported wage limitations when the requests include wages; CPCA 510 admits additional requests following from the main one. The work certificate and pay slips are asked through r6 (labour-disputes 21 ¶3). The notice-period and severance texts are not in the store; costs and interest have no final accessory-requests module to import.

checklist.item: Mandatory prior step: internal grievance procedure inside the employer (Law 90-04, art. 3 to 5) before going to the labour inspectorate.
Mandatory prior step: conciliation before the conciliation office at the labour inspectorate (Law 90-04, art. 19 and following); a record of non-conciliation must be attached to the petition.
Exceptions to prior conciliation: defendant domiciled abroad; employer under judicial settlement or bankruptcy (Law 90-04 art. 19 as amended); check whether the text still says so.
checklist.note: Labour-disputes 19 ¶2 (law 90-04 wording in the store) carries both exceptions; ¶3 takes civil servants out of the conciliation offices.

checklist.item: If a conciliation record (agreement) was drawn up, the claim is replaced by enforcement of the agreement (Law 90-04 art. 33 onward); the court is not seized of the same dispute.
Time limit: the petition must be filed within six months from delivery of the non-conciliation record, under pain of forfeiture of the right of action (CPCM art. 504; also Law 90-04 art. 36?).
checklist.note: CPCA 504 ¶1; labour-disputes 36 sets no period.

checklist.item: How the six months are counted: CPCM art. 405 (full periods, dies a quo not counted, last day extended if holiday), months counted calendar to calendar; who raises the forfeiture (of public order? court of its own motion?).
Lifting of forfeiture by order of the court president for force majeure (CPCM art. 322).
Effect of an earlier non-conciliation record for the same dispute: does a second record restart the six months?
Competent section: the social section of the court (CPCM art. 500); composition with labour assessors (art. 502); if the court has no social section.

Territorial jurisdiction: the court of the place where the work is performed; or the court of the worker's domicile when the contract was suspended or broken by a work accident or occupational disease (CPCM art. 501); this rule is of public order?
checklist.note: CPCA 47 (imported t3) makes the territorial plea one to raise before any defence on the merits.

checklist.item: Judgments in first and last instance for certain labour matters (Law 90-04 art. 21: annulment of disciplinary sanctions, certificates, pay slips), with provisional execution; and appeal otherwise.
checklist.note: Labour-disputes 21 ¶1 to ¶3 (imported b41) and labour-relations 73-4 ¶1, ¶3 and ¶4.

checklist.item: Economic dismissal / reduction of staff (Legislative Decree 94-09, art. 69 to 71 of Law 90-11) is a different regime with its own procedure.
checklist.note: Labour-relations 69 to 71 are not in the store (the labour-relations text view has only 1, 2, 3, 73 to 73-4, 80 and 88). Requested; boundary n4 names the case without citing them.

checklist.item: Resignation, retirement, end of a fixed-term contract, or the worker's abandonment of post are not dismissals; a fixed-term contract concluded outside art. 12 cases is deemed indefinite.
checklist.note: Labour-relations 12, 14 and 66 to 68 are not in the store; requested. The trial period (art. 18, 20: open point o9) and the end of the relationship after a leave to create a business (art. 56 bis 5, law 22-16: open point o12) are named in boundary n4; abandonment of post is open point o14.

checklist.item: Dismissal of a staff delegate or union representative needs special protection (Law 90-14 art. 53 and following): nullity and reinstatement as of right.
checklist.note: Law 90-14 was repealed by article 163 of Law 23-02 of 25 April 2023 (Official Journal 2023 issue 29, page 20). Law 23-02 (art. 131, 132, 137 to 142) sets the protection, the prior registered letters and the remedies; it is not in the store (requested): open point o4, grade D.

checklist.item: A dismissal following a criminal prosecution of the worker: the effect of the criminal case on the civil one (the criminal holds the civil in abeyance, CPP art. 4).
checklist.note: The Code of Criminal Procedure is not in the store; the imported exit carries the point with its own open point.

checklist.item: If the employer is a public administrative body and the worker a civil servant, the claim leaves the ordinary courts (CPCM art. 800-801); if the employer is a public body under private law with contract workers, the social section stays competent.
Limitation of wage claims: periodic renewable rights, five years (Civil Code art. 309); some claims by workers for wages: one year (Civil Code art. 311?).
checklist.note: The one-year period is civil-code 312 ¶3, not 311. For the dismissal claim itself no text sets a period (o1).

checklist.item: Formal notice is not required before a dismissal claim (no contractual default); check whether the formal-notice module applies to the damages request.
checklist.note: Not imported, as in both derivations: 73-4 has the court award the compensation and the prior step is the conciliation attempt; whether 73-4 is a contrary text under civil-code 179 is kept as open point o2.

checklist.item: Documents: non-conciliation record, contract or proof of employment, dismissal decision, pay slips, internal regulation, certificate of social-security affiliation.
Petition formal elements (CPCM art. 15) and the fees: labour petitions by workers may be exempt from judicial fees (Law 90-04 / finance law).
checklist.note: The petition-formal-elements module has no final record to import, so CPCA 15 is cited directly (b13). Labour-disputes 25 (legal aid as of right below twice the guaranteed minimum wage) is imported; no fee-exemption text was found in the store (searched CPCA 17 and the labour-disputes text view).

checklist.item: Amendments to remember: Ordinance 96-21 rewrote art. 73-4 (reinstatement or compensation of at least six months); Law 91-29 rewrote art. 73 to 73-4; CPCM 08-09 (2008) and its 2022 amendment (Law 22-13) on the social section and the specialised courts.
checklist.note: The store gives 73 to 73-3 in the law 91-29 wording and 73-4 in the ordinance 96-21 wording; CPCA 500 to 510 in the law 08-09 wording. The store notes no later amendment of these; CPCA 32 and 800 carry a note on law 22-13 (lines k65 and k67).

checklist.item: Is the plaintiff a worker bound to the defendant by an employment relation (contract, written or not)?
checklist.note: The text that says the relationship arises from a written or unwritten contract and may be proved by any means is not in the store: requested.

checklist.item: What is the legal basis of the right to contest a dismissal and the grounds that make a dismissal lawful?
Was the dismissal for a serious fault, and was the disciplinary procedure followed (notice of hearing, hearing, written decision, reasons)?
checklist.note: The store requires written notification and a hearing; the internal-regulation articles that fix the rest of the procedure are not in the store: requested (open point o7). For a protected worker, Law 23-02 art. 132 and 137 add a prior registered letter (open point o4).

checklist.item: Was the dismissal a collective one for economic reasons, and were its procedures followed?
checklist.note: The articles on reduction of staff are not in the article store. Requested.

checklist.item: Was the dismissal notified in writing, with its reasons, and on what date?
checklist.note: The store requires written notification; it does not say that the reasons must be stated.

checklist.item: Did the worker exhaust the internal procedure of the employer (collective agreement, appeal to the disciplinary body) before going to the conciliation office?
Is conciliation before the labour conciliation office mandatory before filing, and what are its exceptions?
Was a record of non-conciliation drawn up, on what date, and was a record of conciliation reached instead?
Within what time after the record of non-conciliation must the claim be filed, and what is the sanction for filing late?
Is there a limitation period for a claim of abusive dismissal, from what event does it run, and may the court raise it itself?
checklist.note: No special period for dismissal claims was found; the general limitation and that of a harmful act are imported, and neither is applied by the court of its own motion (civil-code 321, imported periods.b23).

checklist.item: Before which court and which section is the claim filed (social section)?
Which court has territorial jurisdiction (place of work, place of contract, domicile of the employer)?
Does the case leave the ordinary courts (public employer, administrative court, criminal court)?
Is the claim heard at first instance and final, or open to appeal, and what are the thresholds?
checklist.note: The store says the court rules at first and last instance (73-4 ¶1 and ¶3, labour-disputes 21) and that cassation is open (73-4 ¶4); no amount threshold appears.

checklist.item: What may the worker ask: reinstatement with the previous rights, and if the employer refuses, compensation?
How is compensation calculated, is there a minimum, and may it be combined with the notice indemnity and the severance indemnity?
checklist.note: Minimums come from 73-4 ¶1 and ¶3; the severance-indemnity and notice-indemnity articles are not in the store: requested.

checklist.item: May the worker also claim unpaid wages, leave pay, notice indemnity, and damages for the manner of dismissal?
checklist.note: Unpaid wages may be added (CPCA 510) and bring the wage limitations; wages alone belong to unpaid-wages (n5). 73-4 ¶3 reserves further compensation (r3, o6). Nothing on notice indemnity or leave pay on dismissal is in the store.

checklist.item: Who must prove the existence of the employment relation, and who must prove the serious fault?
What documents must be attached: contract, work certificate, pay slips, dismissal letter, non-conciliation record?
Is a formal notice required before the claim?
checklist.note: None of the labour texts in the store asks for a formal notice; the prior step is the conciliation record. The civil-code 179 question is kept as open point o2.

checklist.item: What must the petition state (names, capacity, address of both parties, facts, requests)?
Is the worker exempt from court fees in labour claims?
checklist.note: The store gives legal aid as of right to a worker whose pay is below twice the guaranteed minimum wage; no general fee exemption was found.

checklist.item: Is provisional execution available for the judgment, and for which part?
Does a probationary period or a fixed-term contract change the rules on the dismissal?
checklist.note: The articles on the trial period (labour-relations 18 and 20, Official Journal 1990 issue 17 pages 564-565) and on fixed-term contracts are not in the store. Requested; the trial period is open point o9 and boundary n4.

checklist.item: Does a dismissal of a staff delegate or a protected worker follow special rules?
checklist.note: The protection of union delegates and representatives is in Law 23-02 art. 131 and following (Official Journal 2023 issue 29), not in the store. Requested; open point o4.

checklist.item: Is the employer a public body whose staff are governed by the public-service statute?
How are the days of a procedural period counted, and do they run during judicial holidays?
checklist.note: CPCA 405 counts the six months (imported); non-working days inside the period count (405 ¶2). No text on judicial holidays was found in the store.

checklist.item: Is there a pending criminal complaint on the same facts?
Can the defendant be a successor employer after a transfer of the business?
checklist.note: Labour-relations 74 (Official Journal 1990 issue 17 page 569: the relationships continue with the new employer) is not in the store. Requested; open point o11.

checklist.item: What facts must the lawyer ask the client before drafting?

The store notes on civil-code 124 that the temporal start of its wording is unsettled (the introducing text sets no national commencement date; civil-code 4 gives a per-locality rule): from which date does the wording apply, and what does that change for this claim?
checklist.note: Civil-code 124 is cited only for the interpretive reading of further compensation (b14, o6). The note bears on the wording that governs a harmful act done before the amending law took effect; for this claim that is a dismissal before that date, which the imported fifteen-year limitation items (periods.d1, periods.d2) would already warn about. It changes no rule of this record.

checklist.item: The store notes on civil-code 133 that its text is a current snapshot whose commencement bounds are not settled: from which date does the wording apply, and what does that change for this claim?
checklist.note: Civil-code 133 enters through the imported periods.d2 and periods.b28. The note sets no date and records no other wording in the store; the fifteen-year period is the same in the only wording held. It changes nothing for this claim; the module carries the point.

checklist.item: The store notes on civil-code 3 that the Civil Code's inventory and amendment chain are not certified: what does that change for the counting of the imported limitation periods?
checklist.note: Civil-code 3 (Gregorian calendar) is part of the counting basis of the imported periods.d1 to d4; the note names no other wording and no date. It changes nothing for this claim beyond what the periods module already records (its open point on counting years).

checklist.item: The store notes on CPCA 32 that law 22-13 sets no calendar commencement and defers the new jurisdiction rules to the installation of the new courts: from which date does the amended wording apply, and what does that change for this claim's section?
checklist.note: Both wordings of CPCA 32 in the store have the same paragraphs 1 to 6; law 22-13 article 14 ¶2 repealed only paragraphs 7 to 10 (the specialised poles). The paragraphs the section rule rests on (¶4 listing by nature, ¶5 courts without sections, ¶6 referral) read the same whichever wording applies.

checklist.item: The store notes on CPCA 536 مكرر that law 22-13 defers the specialised commercial courts' jurisdiction to their installation: what does that change for a dismissal claim against an employer in bankruptcy or judicial settlement?
checklist.note: Law 22-13 article 13 ¶1 applies the new jurisdiction rules of the specialised commercial courts only from the installation of the new courts, and ¶2 keeps earlier-filed cases with the former courts. Whether such a court is installed for the place is not in the store; the imported exit x5 warns and open point o3 keeps the question.

checklist.item: The store notes on CPCA 800 that law 22-13 defers the new administrative jurisdiction rules to the installation of the new courts: what does that change for a dismissal claim against a public body?
checklist.note: The amended CPCA 800 ¶2 adds national public institutions and national professional organisations to the parties that bring a case before the administrative courts; under law 22-13 article 13 that wording applies from the installation of the new courts. The imported exit x1 and boundary n7 warn on a public party; the modules keep the date question open.

checklist.item: Neighbour flag f-b13-previous: labour-disputes 20 ¶1 (the social courts hear the matters listed, 'with due regard to article 7 of the code of civil procedure').
checklist.note: The paragraph is cited by the imported court-sections.b14 (labour-disputes 20 ¶1 and ¶2), a basis of the section rule. The article 7 it refers to is of the former code of civil procedure, which is not in the store; CPCA 500 now gives the social section its exclusive matters.

checklist.item: Neighbour flag f-b14-previous: labour-disputes 21 ¶1 (except for the original jurisdiction, the social courts rule at first and last instance where the claim is mainly about the listed matters).
checklist.note: The paragraph is cited by the imported labour-prelitigation.b41 (labour-disputes 21 ¶1 to ¶3), the basis of boundary n2 and request r6. Labour-disputes 22 ¶5, which B cited after it, is imported as labour-prelitigation.b58.

checklist.item: Does a strike-related dismissal follow the law on the right to strike (lawful strike, direct contribution, formal notice to resume work)?
checklist.note: Law 23-08 (Official Journal 2023 issue 42) is not in the store; requested. Open point o8.

checklist.item: Is the employer an operator in a free zone whose employment relations are left to freely concluded contracts?
checklist.note: Law 22-15 art. 18 (Official Journal 2022 issue 49) is not in the store; requested. Open point o13.

checklist.item: Does the employer claim abandonment of post, and were formal notices to resume work sent?
checklist.note: No text in the store and no Supreme Court decision found on the court's site; open point o14 (grade D).

message.ar: المادتان 19 و37 من قانون تسوية النزاعات الفردية في العمل: يجب أن يكون كل خلاف فردي في العمل موضوع محاولة صلح أمام مكتب المصالحة قبل مباشرة أي دعوى قضائية، وترفق العريضة بنسخة من محضر عدم المصالحة. وقضت المحكمة العليا (الغرفة الاجتماعية، الملفان 1158046 و1340230) بأنه لا تقبل الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في غياب محضر عدم مصالحة، وأثارت ذلك تلقائيا. تحقق من وجود المحضر ومن تاريخ تسليمه السابق لتاريخ العريضة، أو من قيام إحدى حالات الإعفاء.
message.en: Articles 19 and 37 of the law on individual labour disputes: every individual labour dispute must go through a conciliation attempt before the conciliation office before any court action, and the petition is accompanied by a copy of the non-conciliation record. The Supreme Court (social chamber, files 1158046 and 1340230) held that a claim before the social section is not admissible without a non-conciliation record, and raised the point of its own motion. Check that the record exists and was delivered before the petition's date, or that an exemption applies.

priorSteps.interpretiveNote: Article 19 states the duty and article 37 requires the copy of the record; neither states the sanction of a petition filed without it. The Supreme Court's social chamber supplies it: «لا تقبل الدعوى أمام القسم الإجتماعي في غياب محضر عدم مصالحة» (file 1158046, 07-09-2017), raised of its own motion as «مخالفة قاعدة جوهرية في الإجراءات», and again in file 1340230 (05-03-2020) on articles 19, 36 and 37. That is case law, so the step stays interpretive: it warns, naming the inadmissibility, and never blocks. The step counts as done only when the record exists and was delivered before the petition's date (19 ¶1: before any court action): with the delivery date unknown the step asks for it, and with a delivery on or after the petition's date the step leaves the answer to boundary n5.

message.ar: المواد 2 و4 و5 من قانون تسوية النزاعات الفردية في العمل: النزاع الفردي خلاف لم يحل في إطار التسوية الداخلية، ولا يخطر العامل مفتش العمل إلا بعد استنفاد إجراءات المعالجة الداخلية. تحقق من استنفاد هذه الإجراءات إذا كان المدعي هو العامل.
message.en: Articles 2, 4 and 5 of the law on individual labour disputes: an individual dispute is one not resolved by internal settlement, and the worker refers it to the labour inspector after the internal procedure is exhausted. When the worker is the plaintiff, check that this procedure was followed.

priorSteps.interpretiveNote: The texts put the internal procedure before the referral to the labour inspector; they state no consequence for a court claim filed when it was skipped, and they speak only of the worker. Warn; never block.

message.ar: المادة 504 من قانون الإجراءات المدنية والإدارية: ترفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى. وهذا الأجل منصوص عليه في هذا القانون فتسري عليه المادة 405: يمدد إلى أول يوم عمل إذا لم يكن آخره يوم عمل (الفقرتان 3 و4)؛ ولا يقرر القانون 90-04 المتعلق بتسوية النزاعات الفردية في العمل أجلا آخر لرفع الدعوى (المادة 36 منه). وفي آخر يوم قراءتان: (1) يحسب الأجل كاملا فلا يحسب يوم التسليم ولا يوم انقضاء الأجل، فتقبل الدعوى في اليوم الموالي لتمام الستة أشهر (المادة 405 الفقرة 1)، وهي القراءة المعتمدة؛ (2) يحسب يوم التسليم لأنه ليس يوم تبليغ ولا تبليغ رسمي، فينتهي الأجل في اليوم المقابل ليوم التسليم، أي قبل ذلك بيوم (المادة 504 والمادة 405 الفقرة 1، نقطة مفتوحة). الأحوط رفع الدعوى قبل انقضاء الأجل في القراءة الثانية. لا يمنع التصدير النظيف إلا بعد انقضاء الأجل في القراءة التي تنتهي متأخرة وانقضاء هامشه، وينبه قبل ذلك. وإذا لم يوجد في الشهر الأخير اليوم المقابل ليوم التسليم فنهاية الأجل محل قراءتين (نقطة مفتوحة). ويرفع السقوط في حالة القوة القاهرة بأمر من رئيس الجهة القضائية (المادة 322). تحقق من تاريخ تسليم المحضر.
message.en: CPCA, article 504: the claim must be brought before the social section within six (6) months of the delivery of the non-conciliation record, or the right to bring it is forfeited. The period is laid down in this Code, so article 405 governs it: it runs to the next working day when its last day is not one (paragraphs 3 and 4); Law 90-04 on individual labour disputes sets no other period for bringing the claim (its article 36). Two readings exist on the last day: (1) the period is counted in full, neither the day of delivery nor the day it expires counts, so the claim may still be filed on the day after the six months end (article 405, paragraph 1), the reading the record holds; (2) the day of delivery counts, since it is not a day of notification or service, and the period ends on the day matching the day of delivery, one day earlier (article 504 and article 405, paragraph 1; open point). The safe course is to file before the period ends under the second reading. The clean export is blocked only after the later of the two last days and its band have passed; before that the item warns. Where the last month has no day matching the day of delivery, where the period ends is kept with two readings (open point). A forfeiture for force majeure is lifted by the president's order (article 322). Check the date the record was delivered.

message.ar: المادة 504 من قانون الإجراءات المدنية والإدارية: ترفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح تحت طائلة سقوط الحق، ويستثنى من السقوط حالة القوة القاهرة أو الأحداث المؤثرة في السير العادي لمرفق العدالة، ويقدم طلب رفع السقوط إلى رئيس الجهة القضائية المعروض أمامها النزاع ويفصل فيه بأمر على عريضة (المادة 322). ويحسب الأجل وفق المادة 405 لأنه منصوص عليه في هذا القانون، ويمدد إلى أول يوم عمل (الفقرتان 3 و4)، ولا يقرر القانون 90-04 أجلا آخر (المادة 36 منه). وفي آخر يوم قراءتان: لا يحسب يوم التسليم ولا يوم انقضاء الأجل (المادة 405 الفقرة 1، القراءة المعتمدة)، أو يحسب يوم التسليم لأنه ليس يوم تبليغ فينتهي الأجل قبل ذلك بيوم (المادة 504 والمادة 405 الفقرة 1، نقطة مفتوحة). تحقق من تاريخ تسليم المحضر ومن إثبات القوة القاهرة ومن تقديم طلب رفع السقوط.
message.en: CPCA, article 504: the claim must be brought before the social section within six (6) months of the delivery of the non-conciliation record, on pain of forfeiture; force majeure and events affecting the normal working of the courts are excepted, and the request to lift the forfeiture goes to the president of the court before which the dispute is brought, who rules by an order on petition (article 322). The period is laid down in this Code and counted under article 405, running to the next working day (paragraphs 3 and 4); Law 90-04 sets no other period (its article 36). Two readings exist on the last day: neither the day of delivery nor the day the period expires counts (article 405, paragraph 1; the reading the record holds), or the day of delivery counts, since it is not a day of notification, and the period ends one day earlier (article 504 and article 405, paragraph 1; open point). Check the delivery date, the proof of the force majeure, and that the request to lift the forfeiture is made.

description.ar: تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح الأول عن نفس النزاع
description.en: The date the first non-conciliation record for the same dispute was delivered

message.ar: المادة 504 من قانون الإجراءات المدنية والإدارية: ترفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى. وقضت المحكمة العليا (الغرفة الاجتماعية، الملف 1488919) بأن الحق يسقط إذا أصبح محضر عدم الصلح الأول خارج أجل ستة أشهر، وأنه لا يمكن استصدار محضر ثان بعدم الصلح بخصوص نفس النزاع، وأن عدم القبول في هذه الحالة من النظام العام يثيره القاضي تلقائيا (المادة 69). ويحسب الأجل وفق المادة 405 ويمدد إلى أول يوم عمل (الفقرتان 3 و4)؛ وفي آخر يوم قراءتان: لا يحسب يوم التسليم ولا يوم انقضاء الأجل (المادة 405 الفقرة 1، القراءة المعتمدة)، أو يحسب يوم التسليم لأنه ليس يوم تبليغ فينتهي الأجل قبل ذلك بيوم (المادة 504 والمادة 405 الفقرة 1، نقطة مفتوحة). تحقق من تاريخ تسليم المحضر الأول.
message.en: CPCA, article 504: the claim must be brought before the social section within six (6) months of the delivery of the non-conciliation record, or the right to bring it is forfeited. The Supreme Court (social chamber, file 1488919) held that the right is forfeited once the first non-conciliation record is outside the six months, that a second record cannot be obtained on the same dispute, and that this inadmissibility is of public order, raised by the judge of his own motion (article 69). The period is counted under article 405 and runs to the next working day (paragraphs 3 and 4); two readings exist on the last day: neither the day of delivery nor the day the period expires counts (article 405, paragraph 1; the reading the record holds), or the day of delivery counts, since it is not a day of notification, and the period ends one day earlier (article 504 and article 405, paragraph 1; open point). Check the delivery date of the first record.

deadlines.interpretiveNote: Article 504 ¶1 runs the period from «تسليم محضر عدم الصلح» and says nothing of a second record. Counting from the first record rests on the Supreme Court's social chamber (file 1488919, 07-10-2021, read on coursupreme.dz): «يسقط حق العامل في رفع دعواه أمام القسم الاجتماعي، إذا أصبح محضر عدم الصلح الأول خارج أجل ستة أشهر» and «لا يمكن استصدار محضر ثان بعدم الصلح بخصوص نفس النزاع الذي تضمنه المحضر الأول». Case law, so the deadline is interpretive and warns. The last day carries the same two countings as d1 (open point o15).

reading.ar: يحسب الأجل من تسليم المحضر الأول، ولا يفتح المحضر الثاني أجلا جديدا (المحكمة العليا، الملف 1488919).
reading.en: The period runs from the delivery of the first record; a second record does not open a new period (Supreme Court, file 1488919).

reading.ar: يحسب الأجل من تسليم محضر عدم الصلح المرفق بالعريضة، لأن النص لا يميز بين محضر أول وثان.
reading.en: The period runs from the delivery of the record attached to the petition, the text not distinguishing a first from a second record.

description.ar: اليوم الذي يصبح فيه الدين مستحق الأداء.
description.en: The day the debt becomes due.

message.ar: المادة 308 من القانون المدني: يتقادم الالتزام بخمس عشرة (15) سنة من يوم استحقاقه (المادة 315) فيما عدا ما ورد فيه نص خاص، وتحسب المدة وفق المادة 314، ولا تقضي به المحكمة تلقائيا (المادة 321). وتسري هذه المدة أيضا على الريع المستحق على الحائز سيء النية أو على متصرف المال المشاع (المادة 309)، وعلى الحق الذي حرر به سند (المادة 313، محل قراءتين). تحقق من تاريخ الاستحقاق ومن كل انقطاع أو وقف، ومنه عدم أهلية الدائن أو غيابه أو الحكم عليه بعقوبة جنائية ولو كان له نائب قانوني (المواد 316 و317 و318)، ومن وجود نص خاص بمدة أقصر، كدعاوى عقد التأمين والأوراق التجارية والضمان الاجتماعي (نقاط مفتوحة). وطريقة حساب السنوات، وامتداد المدة إذا انتهت في يوم عطلة، وأثر الإعذار أو الرسالة في قطعها، وكفاية تاريخ العقد عن تاريخ الاستحقاق، محل قراءات محفوظة (نقاط مفتوحة).
message.en: Civil Code, article 308: an obligation is time-barred after 15 years from the day it falls due (article 315), save where a special text applies; counted under article 314; the court does not apply it of its own motion (article 321). The same period governs revenue owed by a possessor in bad faith or by the manager of jointly owned property (article 309), and a right for which a written instrument was drawn up (article 313, two readings kept). Check the due date, any interruption or suspension, including the creditor's incapacity, absence or criminal sentence even where he has a legal representative (articles 316, 317, 318), and whether a special text sets a shorter period, such as actions on an insurance contract, on bills and cheques, or social-security disputes (open points). How the years are counted, whether the period runs on when it ends on a holiday, whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it, and whether the contract date can stand in for the due date are kept with their readings (open points).

deadlines.interpretiveNote: Four readings rest under this deadline, kept open on the owner's instruction (verifier, follow-up 1, boundary cases bc5, bc9, bc10, bc11, bc12, bc16). How a year is counted: by the Gregorian calendar (civil-code 3 ¶1) or as a fixed number of days (314 ¶1 'بالايام لا بالساعات'), open point o15. Whether a period ending on a non-working day runs to the next working day (cpca 405 ¶4) or ends on that day (405 ¶1 speaks of the periods 'في هذا القانون'), open point o16. Whether a formal notice by bailiff or a registered letter is an interrupting 'تنبيه' (317 ¶1), open point o8. Whether a contract made less than the period ago shows the claim in time without its due date (315 ¶1), open point o17. The rule follows the protective reading of each: calendar counting with a band widened by the leap days fifteen years can hold, so a fixed count of days also warns; no extension; no interruption by a notice or letter; the due date is asked. Either way an expired period only warns.

reading.ar: تحسب السنوات بالتقويم الميلادي، وتكمل المدة بانقضاء آخر يوم منها ولو كان يوم عطلة، ولا يقطعها الإعذار ولا الرسالة، وتبدأ من تاريخ الاستحقاق الذي يسأل عنه المحامي.
reading.en: Years are counted by the calendar, the period is complete at the end of its last day even if a holiday, a formal notice or a letter does not interrupt it, and it starts on the due date, which the lawyer is asked for.

reading.ar: تحسب السنة بعدد ثابت من الأيام، وتمدد المدة إلى أول يوم عمل إذا انتهت في يوم عطلة، ويقطعها الإعذار بواسطة المحضر أو الرسالة، وتعد الدعوى في أجلها متى كان العقد المنشئ للالتزام أحدث من المدة.
reading.en: A year is a fixed number of days, a period ending on a holiday runs to the next working day, a formal notice by bailiff or a letter interrupts it, and the claim is in time whenever the contract that created the obligation is more recent than the period.

description.en: The day of the harmful act.

message.ar: المادة 133 من القانون المدني: تسقط دعوى التعويض بانقضاء خمس عشرة (15) سنة من يوم وقوع الفعل الضار. تحقق من تاريخ الفعل الضار ومن كل سبب قاطع للمدة (المادتان 317 و318) أو موقف لها، ومنه عدم أهلية المضرور ولو كان له نائب قانوني (المادة 316)، مع مراعاة القراءتين المحفوظتين. وطريقة حساب السنوات، وأثر الإعذار أو الرسالة في قطعها، محل قراءات محفوظة (نقاط مفتوحة). وفي آخر يوم قراءتان: تكمل المدة بانقضاء آخر يوم منها ولو كان يوم عطلة (المادة 314 من القانون المدني، لأن المادة 405 من قانون الإجراءات المدنية والإدارية تخص الآجال المنصوص عليها في ذلك القانون)، وهي القراءة المعتمدة؛ أو تمدد إلى أول يوم عمل موال (المادة 405 الفقرتان 3 و4، نقطة مفتوحة). وانقضاء المدة لا يؤدي إلا إلى تنبيه في القراءتين.
message.en: Civil Code, article 133: the compensation action falls after 15 years from the day of the harmful act. Check the date of the act and any event that interrupted the period (articles 317, 318) or suspended it, including the victim's incapacity even where he has a legal representative (article 316), keeping in mind the two readings recorded. How the years are counted, and whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it, are kept with their readings (open points). Two readings exist on the last day: the period is complete at the end of its last day even if a holiday (Civil Code article 314, since CPCA article 405 speaks of the periods laid down in that Code), the reading the record holds; or it runs to the next working day (CPCA article 405, paragraphs 3 and 4; open point). Under either reading an expired period only warns.

deadlines.interpretiveNote: The article says the action 'falls' (تسقط) and sits outside the limitation section; whether it is a limitation governed by the rules on suspension, interruption and pleading, or a forfeiture, is a reading, and so is who raises it. Either way an expired period is shown as a warning. Three more readings are kept open on the owner's instruction (verifier, follow-up 1, boundary cases bc5, bc9 to bc12): how a year is counted (open point o15), whether a period ending on a non-working day runs to the next working day (o16), and whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it (o8). The rule keeps calendar counting with a band widened by the leap days fifteen years can hold, no extension, and no interruption by a notice or letter.

reading.ar: مدة تقادم تخضع لأحكام الوقف والانقطاع، ولا تقضي بها المحكمة تلقائيا.
reading.en: A limitation period, subject to suspension and interruption, which the court does not apply of its own motion.

reading.ar: أجل مسقط لا يقبل الوقف ولا الانقطاع، وقد يثار تلقائيا إن كان من النظام العام.
reading.en: A forfeiture period that is neither suspended nor interrupted, which may be raised of the court's own motion if of public order.

description.ar: تاريخ استحقاق أقدم أجر مطالب به.
description.en: The date the oldest wage claimed fell due.

message.ar: المادة 312 من القانون المدني: تتقادم بسنة واحدة (1) المبالغ المستحقة للعمال مقابل عملهم، ومن يتمسك بهذا التقادم يحلف أنه أدى الدين، ولا تقضي به المحكمة تلقائيا (المادة 321). تحقق من تاريخ استحقاق كل أجر مطالب به ومن كل سبب قاطع للتقادم (المواد 317 و318 و319) أو موقف له، كمانع يمنع الدائن من المطالبة أو عدم أهليته أو غيابه أو الحكم عليه بعقوبة جنائية دون نائب قانوني (المادة 316)، ومن تحرير سند بالحق (المادة 313، محل قراءتين). مدة الأجور محل قراءتين محفوظتين. وطريقة حساب السنوات، وامتداد المدة إذا انتهت في يوم عطلة، وأثر الإعذار أو الرسالة في قطعها، محل قراءات محفوظة (نقاط مفتوحة).
message.en: Civil Code, article 312: sums owed to workers for their work are time-barred after 1 year; whoever relies on it must swear that he paid, and the court does not apply it of its own motion (article 321). Check the due date of each wage claimed, any act that interrupted the period (articles 317, 318, 319) and anything that suspended it, such as an impediment that kept the creditor from claiming or his incapacity, absence or criminal sentence without a legal representative (article 316), and whether a written instrument was drawn up for the right (article 313, two readings kept). The period for wages is kept with two readings. How the years are counted, whether the period runs on when it ends on a holiday, and whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it are kept with their readings (open points).

deadlines.interpretiveNote: The Civil Code gives two periods that both read on wage arrears: one year for sums owed to workers for their work, and five years for periodic rights including wages. The texts do not say which prevails; the record warns from the shorter one, and d4 warns at five years under both readings. Three more readings are kept open on the owner's instruction (verifier, follow-up 1, boundary cases bc5, bc9 to bc12): how a year is counted (open point o15), whether a period ending on a non-working day, such as a Friday or an official holiday, runs to the next working day (o16), and whether a bailiff's formal notice or a registered letter interrupts it (o8). The rule keeps the earlier last day of each (calendar counting with a band widened by one leap day, no extension, no interruption by a notice or letter), so the item warns under every reading near the last day.

reading.ar: يسري على الأجور التقادم بسنة لأنه نص خاص بأجور العمال، وهو قائم على قرينة الوفاء بدليل يمين المدين.
reading.en: Wages are subject to the one-year limitation, a specific rule for workers' pay resting on a presumption of payment, as the debtor's oath shows.

reading.ar: يسري على الأجور التقادم بخمس سنوات لأنها حقوق دورية متجددة ذكرت صراحة، ولا يسري التقادم بسنة إلا على غير الأجور الدورية.
reading.en: Wages are subject to the five-year limitation, being periodic rights named expressly; the one-year limitation reaches only non-periodic pay.

description.ar: تاريخ استحقاق أقدم أجر مطالب به.
description.en: The date the oldest wage claimed fell due.

message.ar: المادة 309 من القانون المدني: تتقادم المرتبات والأجور بخمس (5) سنوات ولو أقر بها المدين، ولا تقضي به المحكمة تلقائيا (المادة 321). تحقق من تاريخ استحقاق كل أجر مطالب به؛ وما استحق قبل خمس سنوات من رفع الدعوى معرض للدفع بالتقادم. وتحقق من تحرير سند بالحق (المادة 313، محل قراءتين). وطريقة حساب السنوات، وامتداد المدة إذا انتهت في يوم عطلة، وأثر الإعذار أو الرسالة في قطعها، محل قراءات محفوظة (نقاط مفتوحة).
message.en: Civil Code, article 309: salaries and wages are time-barred after 5 years, even if the debtor acknowledged them, and the court does not apply it of its own motion (article 321). Check the due date of each wage claimed; wages that fell due more than five years before filing are exposed to a limitation plea. Check also whether a written instrument was drawn up for the right (article 313, two readings kept). How the years are counted, whether the period runs on when it ends on a holiday, and whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it are kept with their readings (open points).

deadlines.interpretiveNote: Kept open on the owner's instruction (verifier, follow-up 1, boundary cases bc5, bc6, bc7). How five years are counted across a leap day: by the Gregorian calendar (civil-code 3 ¶1), so five years from 28 February end on 28 February, or as a fixed number of days (314 ¶1 'بالايام لا بالساعات'), which ends a day or two earlier (open point o15). Whether a period ending on a non-working day runs on (o16), and whether a formal notice or a letter interrupts it (o8), are kept the same way. Which deadline carries the five years of 309 ¶1 for wages: this one, read from the date of the oldest wage, while the deadline on other periodic rights (d8) stays silent in a wage claim; the boundary cases read 309 ¶1 as one deadline for every periodic right; the period and its start are the same under both, and whether one year or five governs wages is o1. The rule keeps calendar counting with a band widened by the two leap days five years can hold, so a fixed count of days also warns.

reading.ar: تحسب السنوات الخمس بالتقويم الميلادي من يوم الاستحقاق إلى مثله، ويحمل هذا الأجل مدة الأجور وحدها.
reading.en: The five years are counted by the calendar from the due date to the same day, and this deadline alone carries the period for wages.

reading.ar: تحسب السنوات الخمس بعدد ثابت من الأيام دون اعتبار اليوم الكبيس، وتسري مدة الحقوق الدورية المتجددة على الأجور بالأجل نفسه الذي يسري على غيرها.
reading.en: The five years are a fixed number of days, leap days left out, and the period of periodic renewable rights reaches wages through the same deadline as the other periodic rights.
